question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{y\sqrt{x}}{3}, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 3, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{3}{5},$ find $\text{E}[5X-Y].$
question.worked_solution:
We're given $\text{E}[X].$ So, we first need to compute $\text{E}[Y].$

The marginal density function for $Y$ when $0\le y\le 3$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{y\sqrt{x}}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{y}{3}{[\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3/2}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{y}{3}(\frac{2}{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{2y}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the  expected value of $Y$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}y\cdot \frac{2y}{9}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{9}{[\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{2}{9}(9-0) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[5X-Y] & =5\,\text{E}[X]+(-1)\,\text{E}[Y] \\  & =5(\frac{3}{5})+(-1)(2) \\  & =3-2 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
